title: The family computer becomes a portal
teaser: Someone needs the phone line. Finish the download before you give up the chair.

title: Windows 3.0 Program Manager
teaser: Colorful icons made the family PC feel less like office machinery and more like something worth exploring.

title: The first World Wide Web site
teaser: The first site looks almost modest: text, blue links, and an explanation of what the web is supposed to be.

title: NCSA Mosaic browser
teaser: Blue links, pictures inside the page, and a gray frame around the whole thing.

title: Handmade GeoCities homepage
teaser: Tiled stars, a loud title, and an under-construction badge made the page feel visibly owned.

title: Six-digit visitor counter
teaser: You checked the number again. It had gone up by one.

title: Guestbook with six handles and one typo
teaser: Names, timestamps, and one misspelling could make a personal page feel occupied.

title: Previous / random / next Webring bar
teaser: A small navigation strip let one strange site vouch for the next.

title: AIM away message
teaser: Choose a lyric carefully. Your buddy list is going to read it.

title: Hand-built Yahoo directory
teaser: Categories and subcategories made the expanding web feel browsable by subject.

title: AOL promotional CD
teaser: Bright trial discs promised free hours and a setup wizard while quietly taking over the family phone line.

title: Windows 95 Start button
teaser: Want to open a program? Start here. Want to shut down? Start here too.

title: Motorola pager
teaser: The pager goes off. Finding a phone is your next problem.

title: Mixtape cassette
teaser: Pause-button edits and handwritten track lists made every tape a small act of authorship.

title: Sony Discman
teaser: Pick a track, close the lid, and try not to bump the player on the walk home.

title: Blank CD-R spindle
teaser: The rainbow discs waited to become a summer mix, a backup, or a folder of badly labeled MP3s.

title: VHS videocassette
teaser: The label says DO NOT TAPE OVER. Someone in the house means it.

title: Living-room CRT television
teaser: The episode starts at eight. Get the good spot on the sofa.

title: Blockbuster store interior
teaser: Every copy of the new release is gone. Time to walk the shelves again.

title: Arcade cabinet
teaser: Leave a quarter on the cabinet. Somebody else is playing your next game.

title: Sega Genesis six-button controller
teaser: The pad carried fighting-game technique, sports-game trash talk, and console loyalty.

title: Gray Nintendo 64 controller
teaser: Its odd shape and analog stick announced that 3D games would need a different kind of touch.

title: Original PlayStation hardware
teaser: Put the disc in. Keep the memory card somewhere you can find it.

title: Bondi blue iMac G3
teaser: A blue shell on the desk, with the hardware partly visible inside.

title: Sega Dreamcast
teaser: The little VMU had a screen of its own. Keep it with the controller.

title: Y2K response office
teaser: Rows of screens and response teams turned a date change into nightly-news suspense.

title: Hubble launch
teaser: Discovery carries Hubble out of Florida and into orbit.

title: Doom shareware disks
teaser: A disk could bring a new game to a computer that usually held homework.

title: Atomic Purple Game Boy Color
teaser: Clear purple plastic lets you inspect the board before switching the handheld on.

title: Transparent purple N64 controller
teaser: You can see the board through the purple shell. The buttons still need learning.
